goal: When the merge-fallback rung hits a merge conflict, a bounded agent session resolves it and the resolved tree lands only after the same out-of-band re-verification bar, or the run parks preserved with the session's recorded turn/wall usage within its configured bounds.

graders.name: lint
graders.run: uv run ruff check packages/flywheel-worktree packages/flywheel-orchestrator

relevant: packages/flywheel-worktree/src/flywheel_worktree/worker.py -- the merge-fallback rung's conflict outcome (from landing-merge-fallback) is the escalation point; build_merge_submitter threads the new config; module is over 800 lines, use serena symbols
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_policy.py -- [submit] table parsing gains the two bound keys, strict-on-values validation; module is over 800 lines, use serena symbols

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_autopilot.py -- build_repo_invoker and _drive_agent_iteration: the bounded-session pattern to mirror (lazy SDK via flywheel_core._sdk, injectable invoker, turn budget, wall-clock deadline)
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_init_agent.py -- second example of the lazy SDK boundary
docs/configuration.md -- the [submit] table reference; document the two new keys in this same change
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_policy.py -- extend with the new keys' parse/validation coverage; do not weaken existing assertions
constraints: Bounds are config (D-4): [submit] recovery_agent_max_turns (int, default 30; 0 disables the rung) and [submit] recovery_agent_max_wall_seconds (float, default 900.0); at most one resolution attempt per re-driver pass; wrong-typed values raise PolicyError naming the key

Every SDK touch goes through the lazy flywheel_core._sdk boundary inside the session-driving function; importing flywheel_worktree.worker must succeed without claude-agent-sdk installed and no flywheel-worktree module may reference claude_agent_sdk
The session driver is injectable so tests never invoke the real SDK -- mirror build_repo_invoker's seam

The resolved tree is a landing candidate like any other: task command graders, [submit] verify, and the declared held-out gate re-run against it before the base ref moves; failure parks preserved per criterion 3 and counts toward the existing redrive bound per criterion 7

A land from this rung records the agent-resolved rung value on the landing-rung discriminator introduced by landing-merge-fallback; the session's turn/wall usage is persisted queryably on the run's ledger
A session crash or SDK error must not unwind submit -- the run parks preserved (submit MUST NOT raise)
Commit the change (Conventional Commits) before reporting done
non_goals: Do not change the FF, rebase, or merge-fallback rung semantics, the redrive bound, or the human-review queue mechanics
Do not weaken, delete, or modify existing assertions in the pinned test files
No changes to held-out gate internals
The session resolves textual merge conflicts of already-verified DONE work only -- it never edits task source beyond the conflict resolution, never approves gates, never writes lifecycle state
Do not read or write under .flywheel/verification/
edge_cases: recovery_agent_max_turns = 0: no session spawns and the conflict parks exactly as landing-merge-fallback parks it (the criterion-3 disabled leg)
Bound exhaustion without a resolved tree: park preserved (branch ref resolves, worktree exists), usage recorded at or below the configured bound, and the failure counts toward the redrive bound
A resolved tree that fails re-verify must leave the base ref byte-identical with no Landed record -- agent output never lands on its own claim
Recorded usage exceeding the configured bound must fail the behavior test (the bound is enforced, not advisory)
